Finding: HEAD moved two commits past the blueprint baseline
Root Cause: Permission-policy commits added after the blueprint was written
Resolution: Inspected both; tooling config only; no application code affected; retained
Notes: No reset required

Finding: system_configs has no organization_id so every setting is global across tenants including sales.pricing.* which prices real sales
Root Cause: Setting model predates organisation scoping and was never retrofitted
Resolution: Narrowed twice: Phase 1 feature flags and Phase 8 storefront settings each use their own organisation-scoped table rather than extending Setting; sales.pricing.* remains global
Notes: What remains is sales.pricing.* which drives the operational sale path as well as listing defaults so splitting it is operational pricing work; latent while single-tenant and a live money defect on second tenant onboarding

Finding: Six security advisories against league/commonmark 2.8.3 including CVE-2026-71488 and CVE-2026-71478
Root Cause: Advisories disclosed 2026-08-06 after the prior certification run; not a regression
Resolution: composer update league/commonmark --with-dependencies to a patched release
Notes: composer audit now reports no advisories

Finding: MariaDB gates execute against XAMPP MariaDB 10.4.32 not the certified 11.4.2; 10.4 reached end of life June 2024
Root Cause: Test env defaults to 127.0.0.1:3306 which XAMPP serves; the 11.4.2 instance on 3399 is not running
Resolution: Gates re-pointed at 11.4.2 on port 3399; the 42 failures that move exposed are all fixed and the suite is green
Test: Full MariaDB 11.4.2 suite 1575 tests 0 failures 0 errors
Notes: Concurrency claims still to be re-derived on 11.4.2 in Phase 17; what is closed here is that the gate runs on the certified server and passes

Finding: All seven blueprint gap claims relied on for later phases verified correct against source
Root Cause: n/a
Resolution: No corrections required to the blueprint
Notes: Notably better accuracy than the prior readiness audit

Finding: No organisation feature-flag layer existed (blueprint CFG-001)
Root Cause: Settings were global key/value with no per-organisation module concept
Resolution: Added organization_feature_flags table with organization_id NOT NULL and unique (organization_id feature_key); FeatureCatalog defines 31 features and their dependency graph; OrganizationFeatureService resolves with per-organisation caching
Notes: Deliberately not built on system_configs because that table has no tenant column

Finding: No module presets (blueprint CFG-002)
Root Cause: No preset concept existed
Resolution: Five presets: Essentials/Growing Farm/Full Accounting as a strict superset ladder plus Storefront Seller and Procurement Advanced as overlays; additive by default with an explicit exclusive reset
Notes: Superset ladder asserted by test so a farm that grows never loses a screen

Finding: Feature flags could be mistaken for authorization (blueprint SEC-001)
Root Cause: Risk inherent to introducing a flag layer
Resolution: EnsureFeatureEnabled answers only "is this surface offered"; every gated route retains its permission middleware; regression guard asserts an enabled feature still enforces permission
Notes: Gate returns 404 not 403 so a disabled surface stays undiscoverable

Finding: Introducing flags could hide functionality existing customers rely on
Root Cause: An empty flag table resolving to false would disable every module at deploy
Resolution: Absent row resolves to the catalogue default not false; backfill migration enables the entire catalogue for every organisation existing at deploy; idempotent resumable and non-destructive on re-run
Notes: Blueprint §53 requires the rollout to be additive

Finding: PHP 8.4 implicit-nullable deprecation in PigSaleWorkflowBaselineTest::makePig
Root Cause: Pre-existing signature string $ear = null; becomes fatal in PHP 9
Resolution: Changed to ?string; blast radius checked repo-wide and this was the only instance
Test: MariaDB run clean at 42 tests 0 deprecations
Notes: Unrelated to Phase 1; found because the MariaDB filter matched broadly

Finding: Ghana tax defaults outdated for 2026 (blueprint FIN-008); COVID levy still seeded and levies modelled as cascading
Root Cause: GRA abolished the COVID levy and moved VAT/NHIL/GETFund to a shared base from 2026; the seeder docblock still describes the old ~21.9% cascade
Resolution: Added effective-dated tax_profiles and tax_profile_components; GH_VAT_2026_STANDARD charges all three levies on the net for 20.00 on 100.00; the pre-2026 cascading profile is retained effective 2021-05-01 to 2025-12-31 so historical invoices stay explainable
Notes: NOT an external blocker - the client enters their own taxes (percentage or fixed) as configuration; what must be signed off is that the ARCHITECTURE supports configurable taxes which it does. Actual values are a production/client data-entry matter

Finding: No tax profile model existed; tax codes could not express a multi-levy treatment
Root Cause: TaxCodeSeeder expected a tax group that was never built so every caller would have to combine three codes itself
Resolution: TaxProfile groups levies into one selectable treatment; components carry their own rate so correcting a tax code cannot retroactively change a historical profile
Notes: Extends TaxCode rather than replacing it per the preservation rule

Finding: TaxCode::calculateTax used binary floating point for tax
Root Cause: Method predates the codebase money rules
Resolution: Rewritten to take and return decimal strings using bcmath; docblock directs multi-levy work to TaxCalculator
Test: Covered indirectly; zero call sites verified by grep
Notes: Latent not active - the method was never called so no posted figure was wrong

Finding: GhanaTaxProfileSeeder was not idempotent; a second run hit the unique index
Root Cause: updateOrCreate matched effective_from by equality but the date cast stores a time component so the lookup missed and it inserted a duplicate
Resolution: Matched with whereDate instead
Notes: Would have surfaced as a failed deploy on the second seeder run

Finding: Credit notes could reverse todays tax rather than what was originally charged
Root Cause: Recomputing from live configuration rather than reading the transaction snapshot
Resolution: TaxCalculation::toSnapshot and proportion() scale the ORIGINAL charge; a 2024 sale taxed at 21.90 is credited 21.90 in 2026 not 20.00
Notes: Crediting 20.00 against a 21.90 charge would strand 1.90 of tax permanently

Finding: Finance dashboard counted domain_events across ALL organisations while adjacent counts were scoped
Root Cause: pending_events and failed_events omitted the organisation filter that drafts_awaiting and posted_last_30 both had; domain_events does carry organization_id so this was an omission not a schema limit
Resolution: Scoped both counts identically to their neighbours
Notes: An accountant saw another farm's failure count and their own figure was wrong; missed by the prior audit despite its CF-P0-005 isolation finding

Finding: Failure states were scattered across four unrelated places with no single queue (blueprint FIN-014)
Root Cause: Failed outbox rows blocked COD completions pending refunds and missing tax config each surfaced somewhere different or not at all
Resolution: NeedsAttentionService consolidates six sources with severity ranking; every item carries a plain-language message and a separate technical detail; items filtered by the permission needed to act
Notes: Blueprint §54 requires technical text never be the primary user message

Finding: Finance navigation built from hardcoded role arrays not permissions (blueprint UX-007 and §26)
Root Cause: Menu predates the permission catalogue and repeats role lists per link
Resolution: FinanceNavigation admits an entry only when feature usable AND permission held AND route registered; Advanced Accounting grouped rather than flat and hidden entirely when empty
Notes: Not yet wired into the sidebar - cut-over is Phase 14 because the new menu targets Phase 4-7 routes that do not exist yet

Finding: Money summary cards from blueprint §22 not built
Root Cause: Each card's data is owned by a later phase; building them now against flows those phases reshape produces rework
Resolution: Built in Phase 7 once Quick Expense Simple Purchase and the cash services existed; FinanceSummaryService derives every figure from posted journal lines
Notes: A card showing a plausible but wrong number is worse than no card because nobody checks it

Finding: No first-class Quick Expense workflow (blueprint FIN-001)
Root Cause: Routine farm spend required the full AP/vendor-invoice structure
Resolution: RecordQuickExpenseService translates farm language into a balanced JournalBatchDraft and posts it through PostingEngine; 21 categories map to the chart of accounts so no user selects a GL code
Notes: Wrapper not a second engine - blueprint SEC-002 names double-posting as the specific risk

Finding: Quick Expense could duplicate on double-tap or retry (prompt §36)
Root Cause: Phones with poor signal are the normal entry device not an edge case
Resolution: Unique idempotency key per organisation checked before posting so a duplicate returns the original expense rather than the engine's duplicate-posting error; form mints a per-render token so back-then-resubmit is also safe
Test: 4 idempotency tests; mutation confirmed exactly those four fail
Notes: PostingEngine's own guard remains as the backstop it was designed to be

Finding: An unmappable expense category would block the user
Root Cause: Chart of accounts may not have a bucket for every farm purchase
Resolution: Routes to 2910 Suspense - Payments and flags needs_reclassification rather than refusing the entry
Notes: Money left the farm regardless; refusing makes the books less accurate not more

Finding: Receipt attachments not wired into Quick Expense
Root Cause: Requires extending the shared finance attachment subsystem's polymorphic parent support and authorization to a new parent type
Resolution: Deferred to Phase 6 with its own cross-organisation download-refusal tests
Notes: A security-sensitive shared component change not a bolt-on

Finding: Cash bank and MoMo balances were fragmented with no single workspace figure (blueprint FIN-004)
Root Cause: Balances were only reachable through the trial balance and treasury screens
Resolution: MoneyAccountService derives balances by summing posted journal_lines per account - the same rows the trial balance reads - so the cash screen cannot drift from the ledger; mobile money providers stay separate accounts
Notes: Prompt §38 forbids a separate balance source

Finding: No internal transfer workflow; moving money between farm accounts was mis-recordable as an expense (blueprint FIN-011)
Root Cause: A transfer entered as a payment understates profit by the whole amount while the destination balance rises with no matching income
Resolution: RecordCashTransferService requires BOTH legs to be configured money accounts so a revenue or expense account cannot appear in the journal; posts through PostingEngine; idempotent
Notes: The mistake is made structurally inexpressible rather than merely discouraged

Finding: MoneyAccountService resolved a duplicated account code to the wrong row
Root Cause: keyBy('code') keeps whichever row the database returns last and the chart of accounts can hold both a global and an organisation-scoped account with the same code; the ledger posted to id 183 while the screen read id 2 and showed zero
Resolution: Resolve one account per code with the organisation-scoped row always winning
Notes: Found by tracing a failing test rather than adjusting its expectation

Finding: MoneyAccountService silently ignored its $organization argument
Root Cause: Balance lookup went through LedgerBalanceQuery which resolves the tenant from ambient request context
Resolution: Query journal lines directly with the explicit organisation id; still the same single ledger source
Notes: Would have reported one farm's balances against another farm's accounts

Finding: Cash workspace UI cash confirmation and Paystack clearing not built
Root Cause: Money In/Out are views over receipts and payments that Phase 7 reshapes; cash confirmation needs an order to confirm against; clearing needs the storefront integration
Resolution: Money In/Out delivered by the Phase 7 Sales & Money In workspace; Paystack settlement discrepancies surfaced in Needs Attention by Phase 12
Test: MoneyInTest 12 tests and StorefrontFinanceBoundaryTest settlement tests
Notes: Services are the durable part and are complete; screens are cheap once their data settles

Finding: Quick Expense could not hold its receipt (blueprint §23 item 8; deferred from Phase 4)
Root Cause: Wiring it required extending AttachmentController::PARENT_MAP - the shared map that also gates payment receipt invoice and refund evidence and was the site of both CF-P0-004 and CF-P1-019
Resolution: Added a quick-expenses entry with write=record_expenses so a store officer can photograph the receipt without holding view_finance; download still accepts view OR write; QuickExpense gained the morphMany relation
Test: QuickExpenseAttachmentTest 9 tests incl. two cross-organisation refusals
Notes: All 17 attachment tests across the subsystem still pass so no regression to the existing parent types

Finding: Simple Purchase not built; a naive implementation would double-post inventory
Root Cause: InventoryService writes only the subledger - GL posting for a stock receipt is owned by RawMaterialReceivedSubscriber which posts Dr Inventory / Cr GR-IR. A Simple Purchase service also posting Dr Inventory / Cr AP would debit inventory twice per delivery and propagate the error into COGS on every later sale
Resolution: Investigated and design resolved not guessed: Simple Purchase must wrap ReceiveRawMaterialService for stock lines and post no inventory journal of its own; the credit side is the GR/IR clearing account settled by the vendor invoice
Test: Pending - required test is that the inventory control account is debited exactly once per stock purchase
Notes: Blueprint SEC-002 in its most literal form; the next session can build directly from the resolved design

Finding: Simple Purchase service built without double-posting inventory
Root Cause: Design resolved in IMP-029: RawMaterialReceivedSubscriber owns the inventory GL
Resolution: RecordSimplePurchaseService hands stock lines to ReceiveRawMaterialService and posts only the settlement leg which debits the suspense account the subscriber credited; expense lines reuse the Quick Expense category mapping; pay-later requires a supplier
Test: SimplePurchaseTest 16 tests; double-post mutation caught by the governing test alone
Notes: Blueprint SEC-002 avoided by construction rather than by convention

Finding: My governing double-post test was vacuous as first written
Root Cause: It filtered accounts on account_subtype = inventory but every inventory control account in this chart is subtype current_asset so the filter matched nothing and assertCount(0) passed regardless of service behaviour
Resolution: Rewritten to match the 12xx code range and to add a positive assertion that the suspense account is debited 800.00; verified by mutation which now fails exactly this test
Notes: Same class of weak assertion caught in Phase 4; found by checking whether the filter could ever match rather than trusting a green run

Finding: Simple Purchase had no user surface
Root Cause: Service was built first so the accounting could be proven before the form existed
Resolution: Controller routes and mobile-first views with a progressive multi-line form; feature-gated and permission-gated; service exceptions surface as form errors rather than crashes
Notes: Form carries a per-render idempotency token so back-then-resubmit cannot receive a delivery twice

Finding: record_purchases deliberately narrower than record_expenses
Root Cause: A stock line receives goods into inventory which changes stock on hand and flows into COGS on every later sale so it is not the same act as recording that money left the farm
Resolution: Granted to farmmanager and above but NOT dataentry; blueprint §14 and §49 differ on this and the reading that limits who can move stock was chosen
Notes: Can be widened by an administrator far more easily than an inflated inventory can be unwound

Finding: Overview had no money figures
Root Cause: Deferred from Phase 3 until the flows owning each figure existed
Resolution: FinanceSummaryService derives cash available money in money out net customers owing and bills to pay from posted journal lines with no summary table or cached total; sign conventions applied in the service so the view never calls abs()
Test: FinanceSummaryTest 13 tests; sign mutation caught by two tests
Notes: Tests drive the cards through the real Quick Expense and Simple Purchase workflows rather than hand-built journal rows

Finding: MariaDB gates moved to the supported 11.4.2 server and the suite went from passing to 39 errors and 3 failures
Root Cause: The gates had been running on XAMPP MariaDB 10.4.32 which reached end of life June 2024; 12 of the failures are journals_balanced_when_posted_check - the database constraint that enforces double-entry integrity on posted journals
Resolution: Environment fixed: 11.4.2 started on port 3399 with .env.testing.mariadb.local and the safe-DB guard's non-standard-port escape hatch; the 42 failures are now visible and triaged in MARIADB_11_4_GATE_FINDING.md
Notes: Stale-schema hypothesis tested with migrate:fresh and DISPROVED - identical result so these are genuine version behaviours not drift; invalidates any prior claim that the MariaDB gates or concurrency guarantees were proven on 11.4.2

Finding: The Other option on pig death recording is unusable in production - selecting it causes a database constraint violation
Root Cause: RecordPigDeathRequest collapses the free-text disposal_method_other and death_cause_other into the enum columns but pig_deaths CHECK constraints only permit the fixed value lists so any free-text value is rejected; invisible because the 3306 test database had drifted from the migrations and carried no such constraints
Resolution: Root-caused and documented; fix deferred as a deliberate behaviour change - keep the enum and stop collapsing so free text stays in its own column preserving the ability to aggregate disposal methods
Notes: Reframes IMP-035: the primary problem was test-database schema drift not the MariaDB version; the version move is what exposed it by forcing a fresh migration

Finding: WHT certificate generation crashed with Unknown column is_primary and could also leak another supplier's billing address
Root Cause: WhtCertificateService queried counterparty_addresses.is_primary but that table has is_default - counterparty_contacts is the table with is_primary which is where the confusion came from; the same block read line1/line2 where the columns are address_line_1/address_line_2 which failed silently; and where(A)->orWhere(B) escaped the relation constraint so the OR branch could match any supplier's billing address
Resolution: Fixed all three: is_default
Status: grouped the or-condition inside a closure
External Dependency: WhtCertificate suites 31 passed on MariaDB 11.4.2 up from 14 errors
column15: Found only because the test database was rebuilt from the migrations; the stale 3306 database never exercised it

Finding: Twelve journals_balanced_when_posted_check failures traced to a broken test helper not to unbalanced application journals
Root Cause: BankReconciliationServiceTest::postJournalToBank defaulted contraDebit and contraCredit to 0.00 and no caller ever passed them so the helper - whose own comment promises the batch balances - wrote posted journals with 1000.00 debit and 0.00 credit; the stale 3306 database had no such constraint so it was never noticed
Resolution: Contra side now mirrors the bank side unless a caller overrides it; bank-side lines untouched so the book-balance arithmetic the tests assert is preserved
Test: BankReconciliationServiceTest 11 passed on 11.4.2 with zero balance violations
Notes: Good news: the application was never posting unbalanced journals - PostingEngine's own validation prevents it - the defect was confined to a fixture

Finding: Recording a pig sale with purpose Export causes a database constraint violation
Root Cause: RecordPigSaleRequest validates sale_purpose in market/breeding/slaughter/EXPORT/other but the pig_sales CHECK constraint permits market/breeding/slaughter/CULL/other - the two lists disagree on one value each so Export passes validation then is rejected by the database; the sale_purpose_other collapse may be a second issue in the same field
Resolution: NOT FIXED - requires a business decision on whether the farm sells for export or records culls; guessing would either hide a real sale category or invent one
Notes: Third production defect found by rebuilding the test database from migrations; PigSale::getSalePurposeBadge and getSalePurposeIcon both handle export and neither handles cull which suggests the application is right and the constraint is wrong

Finding: Export pig sales rejected by the database - FIXED
Root Cause: Validation allowed export while the CHECK constraint allowed cull; the two lists disagreed on one value each
Resolution: Corrective migration widens the constraint to include export while RETAINING cull since widening cannot break existing data but narrowing can; cleared 7 of the 8 pig_sales failures
Test: PigSaleWorkflowBaselineTest 13 tests 1 remaining error from a separate cause
Notes: Applied on the user's instruction; display helpers had an export arm and no cull arm which is what tipped the decision

Finding: The Other option remains broken on pig deaths and pig sales and my recommended fix was based on a false assumption
Root Cause: I recommended keeping the enum and letting free text live in its own _other column - but neither pig_deaths nor pig_sales HAS such a column so there is nowhere to store the text; the request classes collapse free text into the enum column because that is the only column there is
Resolution: NOT FIXED - the correct fix is larger than described: add death_cause_other disposal_method_other and sale_purpose_other columns by migration then stop collapsing and update every display path; alternative is dropping the CHECK constraints and losing the ability to aggregate
Test: 7 remaining constraint failures all from this one cause
Notes: Correction to my own earlier recommendation - I asserted the columns existed without checking

Finding: A security test's write-check assertion targeted a column that does not exist so it never evaluated
Root Cause: FinanceRouteAuthorizationTest::test_bank_account_creation_is_denied_without_permission asserted assertDatabaseMissing on bank_accounts.name but the column is label; on MariaDB the assertion errored rather than passing or failing so the "and nothing was written" half of the test was never exercised and assertForbidden carried it alone
Resolution: Corrected to label in both the payload and the assertion
Notes: The security property itself was still enforced by the 403 - but a test that cannot evaluate its own assertion is not evidence of the thing it claims to prove

Finding: The Other option on pig death recording is fixed
Root Cause: The request collapsed free text into the CHECK-constrained enum column because there was nowhere else to put it
Resolution: Added nullable death_cause_other and disposal_method_other columns; the request now keeps the enum value and sends the text separately; RecordPigDeathService persists both; PigDeath accessors surface the free text on read when the enum says other so NO view needed changing
Test: PigDeathWorkflowBaselineTest 5 passed on 11.4.2 and 13 death tests pass on SQLite
Notes: Existing tests asserting the collapsed display value pass unchanged which is what proves the accessor preserves every read site; pig_sales needs the same treatment

Finding: Every storefront pig sale failed to post to finance on a correctly-constrained database
Root Cause: StorefrontOrderConfirmedSubscriber writes sale_purpose => storefront but that value appeared in no CHECK constraint allowlist so the INSERT was rejected and the sale spine broke at the subscriber; invisible because the 3306 test database carried no constraint and SQLite never had one
Resolution: Constraint widened to include storefront preserving existing behaviour
Notes: Open question for the business: storefront is arguably a CHANNEL not a purpose and pig_sales already has sales_channel_id - emitting market instead would be the cleaner model but would restate how every historical storefront sale is categorised in reports

Finding: The Other option on pig sales is fixed
Root Cause: Same collapse defect as pig deaths - RecordPigSaleService overwrote sale_purpose with the free text which the CHECK constraint rejects
Resolution: sale_purpose keeps its constrained value; sale_purpose_other holds the text; PigSale accessor surfaces it on read so no call site changed; payment_method left alone because it carries no CHECK constraint
Notes: Same three-step pattern proven on pig deaths first

Finding: Storefront pig sales now record sale_purpose=market with the channel modelled separately
Root Cause: First fix widened the CHECK constraint to accept storefront which preserved existing behaviour; the storefront and finance modules are NOT in production so there is no history to protect and the clean model is available
Resolution: Subscriber emits market; storefront removed from the constraint allowlist; the channel stays recoverable through storefront_order_items.posted_sale_id and matches how the feed path already passes channel as its own field
Test: All 124 storefront tests pass on MariaDB 11.4.2
Notes: Superseded IMP-044 once the user confirmed these modules are pre-production

Finding: Tax settings UI not built so a client cannot enter their own taxes
Root Cause: Phase 2 built the tax engine and profiles but deferred the settings surface
Resolution: Built: Finance > Tax lets a client define profiles and charges as percentage OR fixed amount with optional compounding; the preview computes on GHS 100 using the REAL TaxCalculator so the screen cannot diverge from what a sale posts
Notes: Permission manage_tax_settings is distinct per prompt §119 and granted to admin superuser accountant; route is NOT feature-gated so a farm on Essentials can still configure tax

Finding: Eight tests errored trying to persist an org-less user which users.organization_id NOT NULL forbids
Root Cause: A single setUp fixture in OrganizationScopePolicyTest used User::forceCreate with organization_id null which failed the whole class - five of the eight failures were unrelated tests taking collateral damage from one line
Resolution: Build the org-less user as an UNSAVED model instead; the policy and middleware branches guarding that state are still exercised without asserting the database permits a row it rejects
Test: 12 tests pass on MariaDB 11.4.2; suite errors 13 to 5
Notes: The defensive code is worth keeping - it guards a model hydrated from a raw query or a future nullable column - but persisting the fixture claimed something the schema forbids

Finding: Three more fixtures omitted organization_id entirely rather than passing null
Root Cause: users.organization_id is NOT NULL so an insert with no such key errors with Field doesn't have a default value - a DIFFERENT error from cannot be null and one that only appears on a database carrying the constraint
Resolution: Fixed FinanceSidebarNavigationTest and FinanceReadinessMigrationsTest to resolve or create an organisation for their user fixtures
Test: FinanceSidebarNavigationTest 3 passed and FinanceReadinessMigrationsTest 7 passed on 11.4.2
Notes: Two DerivedOrganizationScopeTest mating tests remain - a different fixture inserting pigs_management with a null organisation

Finding: Business decision: retain cull in the pig sale purpose list
Root Cause: I had kept it defensively because narrowing a CHECK constraint can reject existing rows and flagged it for removal once the user confirmed the modules are pre-production
Resolution: DECIDED BY CLIENT - keep it. Other farms may need cull at the commercial level so it stays a first-class purpose not a legacy artefact
Notes: No code change required; current allowlist is market breeding slaughter cull export other

Finding: Business decision: retain the seeded pre-2026 Ghana tax profile
Root Cause: I had flagged it as possible clutter once clients define their own taxes since with no production data there are no historical invoices to explain
Resolution: DECIDED BY CLIENT - keep it. Seed data is a starting point and can always be changed through the tax settings screen
Notes: No code change required; also serves as a worked example of a compounding profile which the settings screen otherwise has no demonstration of

Finding: All thirteen storefront feature flags were enforced nowhere - a farm could switch Manure Sales off and keep selling manure switch Paystack off and keep taking card payments and switch the whole store off and stay open
Root Cause: Phase 1 built the flag layer and the storefront predates it; no route middleware service or view ever consulted a storefront flag and StorefrontSettings::enabled() had zero callers
Resolution: StorefrontCatalog maps kind to flag and payment method to flag in one place; public shop cart checkout quote flow and listing detail all enforce it; EnsureStorefrontOpen closes the shop; CheckoutService repeats the payment and fulfilment checks the form request makes
Test: StorefrontSettingsEnforcementTest 18 tests; reintroducing the defect fails 7 of them
Notes: A configuration the application does not honour is worse than no configuration - an administrator reads the screen and believes it

Finding: Storefront settings were global across tenants - one store name one support email one pickup address for every farm on the installation
Root Cause: StorefrontSettings read the storefront.* namespace from system_configs which has no organization_id (IMP-001)
Resolution: New storefront_settings table one row per organisation organization_id NOT NULL with a unique index; StorefrontSettingsResolver singleton resolves and caches per organisation; backfill carries the old global values onto every organisation idempotently
Notes: Closes the storefront half of IMP-001; sales.pricing.* remains open because it also drives the operational sale path

Finding: Blueprint §34 lists payment methods categories delivery and guest checkout as settings while §32 lists them as feature flags - implementing both would give one behaviour two switches
Root Cause: Two blueprint sections describing the same controls from different angles
Resolution: The settings screen WRITES the feature flags rather than duplicating them; storefront_settings holds only the values a flag has no room for; a test asserts the duplicate columns do not exist
Notes: An administrator who turns COD on in one place and finds it still off in the other is the failure mode being avoided

Finding: Using the storefront.enabled flag as the day-to-day open/closed sign would destroy a farm's configuration
Root Cause: Every storefront flag declares requires storefront.enabled and disable() cascades to dependants by design - unticking store enabled would switch off Paystack COD delivery quotes accounts and all six category flags with no way to restore them
Resolution: public_shop_open is a settings column; StorefrontSettings::enabled() requires the module flag AND the column; the Modules screen owns whether a shop exists and the settings screen owns whether it is open
Notes: The two are genuinely different questions not a duplicated switch

Finding: Delivery had no destination-based pricing - the only fee was per listing so one journey was charged once per animal in the order
Root Cause: Blueprint §34 lists delivery zones/fees as new; the existing model charges by what is bought not where it goes
Resolution: storefront_delivery_zones with organisation-scoped unique names; when a farm has active zones the buyer picks one and its fee IS the delivery fee with per-listing fees ignored; with no zones the previous behaviour is unchanged; orders snapshot delivery_zone_name so a later re-price still explains an old order
Test: StorefrontSettingsEnforcementTest 5 zone tests including 500.00 plus 85.50 equals 585.50 not 605.50
Notes: Zone id is re-read and organisation-scoped inside checkout - a posted zone id is buyer input like any other

Finding: A closed shop answering 404 would be a dead end for members of the public with no other way in
Root Cause: EnsureFeatureEnabled returns 404 which is right for a finance module but wrong for a shop that is temporarily not selling
Resolution: EnsureStorefrontOpen renders a closed page naming the farm with its phone and email at 503 so crawlers treat the closure as temporary; the Paystack webhook and callback are deliberately NOT closed so money already in flight still settles
Notes: Blueprint §46 no dead ends

Finding: The settings resolver cache was invalidated only by its own save() so a direct model write left a stale read within one request
Root Cause: Resolver caches per organisation for the request; seeders console tooling and tests write the model directly
Resolution: StorefrontSetting and StorefrontDeliveryZone forget the resolver on saved and deleted so any writer is covered; the manual forget() calls papering over it in two tests were removed so those tests now prove the invalidation works
Notes: Invisible in production - one request one container - which is what made it worth fixing rather than working around

Finding: The last two MariaDB gate failures were a fixture that confused two columns not the org-less pattern recorded
Root Cause: DerivedOrganizationScopeTest set matings.status to pending but that is a valid pregnancy_status; matings.status is enum planned/completed/cancelled/failed so MariaDB truncated and errored while SQLite which has no enum passed
Resolution: Fixture uses planned; both tests assert organisation derivation and cross-tenant visibility so any valid status serves; not a production defect - no application path writes pending to that column
Test: Full MariaDB 11.4.2 suite 1575 tests 0 failures 0 errors
Notes: MariaDB 11.4.2 gate is now at zero - 42 down to 0

Finding: Seventeen of twenty finance feature flags were enforced nowhere - FinanceNavigation hid the menu entries while every URL stayed live
Root Cause: Phase 1 built the flag layer and the finance surfaces predate it; only overview quick_expense and simple_purchase carried feature middleware
Resolution: Gated the three Phase 7 flags on their route groups - sales_money_in over invoices receipts feed-sales credit-notes and money-in; contacts over customers suppliers and statements; loans over loans. Advanced flags recorded for Phase 14 rather than done piecemeal
Test: MoneyInTest ContactsWorkspaceTest LoansOwnerViewTest CreditNoteScreenTest feature-off tests
Notes: Prompt §110 - a disabled feature must not remain usable via URL

Finding: Credit notes had no user surface at all
Root Cause: CreditNoteService and SalesReturnRevenueSubscriber have created numbered credit notes since the sales-return work but nothing in the application ever displayed one - a farm could reverse revenue and credit a customer with no way to see it happened
Resolution: Finance > Credits: list detail and a customer-facing PDF. Deliberately read-only - §29 anchors the idempotency key to the sales return that caused the credit so a screen that minted them directly would allow revenue reversed with no return and a second reversal for the same goods
Test: CreditNoteScreenTest 6 tests including a route-table walk asserting every credit-note route is GET-only
Notes: The sales-return UX that creates them is §43 in Phase 13

Finding: No one-button payment - blueprint §28 asks for record payment from the invoice and automatic allocation and neither existed
Root Cause: Taking money against an invoice meant opening Receipts starting a new receipt picking the customer typing the amount ticking auto-allocate and trusting FIFO landed it on the right invoice
Resolution: MoneyInController orchestrates ReceiptService::createPosted then AllocationService::allocate and posts no journal of its own; allocation is TARGETED at the chosen invoice not FIFO because the farmer pressed the button on a specific row
Test: MoneyInTest 12 tests; reintroducing FIFO fails one and a second posting path fails another
Notes: Closes IMP-027 Money In / Money Out deferred from Phase 5

Finding: Customers and suppliers were two unrelated screens though they are one table
Root Cause: counterparties has type with a both value and customers()/suppliers() scopes - the split was never in the data only in the UI
Resolution: Finance > People & Businesses with Customers Suppliers and Balances tabs guided creation and search; the accountant-grade detail screens are kept and linked to
Notes: Blueprint §27

Finding: A unified who-owes-what summary would have routed around an existing permission boundary
Root Cause: finance/ageing/ap requires view_ap_ageing while finance/ageing/ar requires only view_finance - showing both sides of the Balances tab to everyone would have widened access without anyone deciding to
Resolution: The AP side is built only for users holding view_ap_ageing and the tab says plainly when it is withheld
Notes: Caught while designing the tab not after

Finding: Guided contact creation could have let manage_customers create suppliers
Root Cause: One form with a role selector means the screen no longer implies the permission
Resolution: The chosen ROLE decides which permissions are required and the controller checks each one; both is refused unless the user holds both
Notes: A supplier is who the farm pays

Finding: No customer-facing invoice or receipt document existed
Root Cause: Only WHT certificates and account statements rendered as PDFs - a farm could raise an invoice take the money and issue a credit note with nothing to give the person on the other side
Resolution: CustomerDocumentRenderer produces invoice receipt and credit-note PDFs; each states on its face when it is cancelled reversed or unposted so a document that looks payable when it is not cannot be handed over
Notes: Blueprint §28 and §29

Finding: StatementPdfRenderer reads its company block from environment config so on a second tenant one farm's documents would carry another farm's name and TIN
Root Cause: config(finance.statements.company_*) is installation-wide - the same IMP-001 defect in a different table
Resolution: The new customer documents read the organizations row with the env values kept as fallback so a single-tenant install configured the old way still prints the same header; StatementPdfRenderer itself is unchanged and recorded
Notes: Statements still read env config - narrowing IMP-001 further is its own change

Finding: Loans were presented as a liability register not as money to pay back
Root Cause: Reference lender type principal outstanding in a table with the schedule reachable only inside one loan's amortisation view - the question an owner asks first (when is the next payment due) was the hardest thing to find
Resolution: Owner list leads with still-to-pay-back across active loans and the next six scheduled payments with overdue flagged; the detail page keeps amortisation and accrued interest unchanged
Notes: Blueprint §26

Finding: Eleven of twelve MoneyInTest tests failed with 403 because the shared finance fixture's user holds a role with no permission grants
Root Cause: FinanceTestSetup creates an admin-role user but the permission seeders had not run - refusal assertions written the other way round would have passed for the wrong reason
Resolution: Seeded the real permission seeders and used role-backed users so the tests exercise the same role-to-permission map production ships with
Notes: A permission test that passes because everything is forbidden proves nothing

Finding: NavigationHelper::sidebarSections() still builds a hardcoded role-based finance menu in parallel with FinanceNavigation
Root Cause: Phase 3 added FinanceNavigation but did not remove the legacy sidebar builder
Resolution: Recorded not fixed - found because the legacy sidebar links to loan reclassification regardless of the feature flag which made a Phase 7 assertion match the wrong element
Notes: Two menu builders means two places a gating rule has to be remembered

Finding: Guest checkout did not exist though blueprint §17 lists it as essential storefront scope
Root Cause: storefront_carts.user_id was NOT NULL CartService took User in every method and every cart and checkout route sat behind auth:sanctum - a buyer had to register before putting anything in a basket
Resolution: Cart is a database row addressed by an opaque 64-hex cookie token; CartOwner models a guest as a different kind of owner rather than a missing user; cart and checkout routes moved to the public shop prefix
Notes: Session-held carts were rejected because Laravel rotates the session on login - exactly when a buyer has a full basket

Finding: Attaching guest orders by email match at registration would hand a stranger's order history to anyone registering with their address
Root Cause: §38 asks for optional account creation after order and this application does not prove email ownership before login
Resolution: Each guest order carries a single-use guest_claim_token delivered in the confirmation URL; claiming requires presenting it and the token is cleared on use so a forwarded link cannot be replayed against a second account
Test: GuestCheckoutTest test_a_claim_token_cannot_be_replayed; reintroducing the defect fails it
Notes: Decision confirmed by the client before implementation

Finding: A guest order lookup could have become a way to read every order in the system
Root Cause: An order tracking page addressed by reference alone is readable by anyone who can count; comparing a secret in the WHERE clause is a timing oracle and on some collations a case-insensitive match
Resolution: locate() requires reference AND token compares with hash_equals in PHP and uses get() not first() because the reference is unique per organisation not globally so two farms can both hold SO-0001
Test: GuestCheckoutTest test_an_order_cannot_be_read_without_its_token; reintroducing the defect fails it
Notes: The cross-tenant reference collision was caught in review not by a test failing

Finding: Guest counterparty matching by phone would post one person's order onto another person's ledger
Root Cause: Phone numbers are shared within households and re-issued by networks
Resolution: Matching is by email only - the same rule registered buyers already follow; a guest with no email gets a fresh counterparty because a duplicate contact record is a tidy-up job and a wrong match is someone else's purchase history
Notes: A guest order still needs a counterparty - no account means no User never no counterparty

Finding: A guest who signed in mid-purchase would lose the basket they had just filled
Root Cause: The cart was keyed on user_id so a guest cart had nowhere to go on login
Resolution: mergeGuestCartInto adds quantities and caps a merged line at what is still available rather than dropping it so the buyer keeps what they can have and finds out now rather than at checkout
Notes: Blueprint §46 - losing a basket at the moment of commitment is the dead end the no-dead-end rule exists for

Finding: Checkout became an unauthenticated POST and carried no rate limit
Root Cause: It was behind auth before so throttling was unnecessary
Resolution: Ten a minute keyed by user id where there is one so several buyers behind one office NAT do not throttle each other; each attempt mints an order reference and can create a counterparty
Notes: Joins quote submission and the Paystack webhook as a throttled public surface

Finding: An existing test asserted that the cart and checkout redirect a guest to /login
Root Cause: OrderHttpTest::test_cart_and_checkout_require_auth encoded the behaviour §17 calls wrong
Resolution: Rewritten to assert the intended behaviour rather than deleted so the file still covers that surface
Notes: A test that passes because the product is wrong is worse than no test

Finding: Nothing happened to inventory between checkout and staff confirmation so two buyers could both pay for the last animal
Root Cause: Confirmation locking protects the farm's inventory but not the buyer's money - by the time it refuses the losing customer has already been sent to Paystack and may have paid
Resolution: storefront_inventory_holds claims stock inside the checkout transaction under the same row lock the confirmation path takes; the second checkout blocks then reads the first buyer's hold and is refused before any money moves
Test: HoldServiceTest 17 tests; HoldConcurrencyTest 4 multi-process tests on MariaDB 11.4.2
Notes: Blueprint §37 states the problem exactly

Finding: A held listing state cannot express a partial quantity
Root Cause: Blueprint §36 offers either a held state or a holds table; a listing with ten bags and a hold on two is not held - it is eight sellable and two spoken for so a status column would either block the other eight or protect neither
Resolution: Rows carrying a quantity; the listing state machine is untouched which matters because ListingService enforces legal transitions and other work depends on that table not growing edges

Finding: A hold that decremented stock would take the same units twice
Root Cause: quantity_available is decremented at confirmation; a hold doing the same would subtract softly and then for real and the release path would hand back stock never taken
Resolution: Holds do not move inventory - availableToSell() is the column minus live holds and confirmation consumes the hold in the same transaction that decrements the column so the two never both count

Finding: Cancelling a confirmed order could have handed back stock twice
Root Cause: Cancellation reverses stock through applyInventoryEffect; if it also turned the consumed hold back into a released one the unit would return twice
Resolution: resolve() is scoped to status=active so a consumed hold stays consumed

Finding: Expiring every hold on a clock would fail routine cash orders
Root Cause: §37 puts the clock on payment while a cash order waits on a person and its hold remains until staff decision - a thirty minute expiry would fail COD orders because the farm answered the phone slowly
Resolution: expires_at is set only for orders in pending_payment and left null otherwise; scopeLive handles the null branch explicitly because expires_at > now() alone silently drops every null in SQL and would stop protecting every cash order

Finding: The end-to-end checkout concurrency test passes with the row lock removed
Root Cause: CheckoutService allocates a reference through NumberingService which takes SELECT FOR UPDATE on a per-organisation sequence row so every concurrent checkout for one farm serialises on that row - real protection but entirely incidental and it would vanish the day numbering changed
Resolution: Added a second test that races placeForOrder() directly against pre-created orders with no numbering in the path so the listing lock is the only thing between the workers
Notes: Found by reintroducing the defect and watching the test stay green

Finding: The negative control for the hold row lock is probabilistic not deterministic
Root Cause: With lockForUpdate removed twelve workers DID produce two live holds on one animal - a real observed oversell - but it did not reproduce on demand; the workers that overlapped were the slow ones at 124ms and 159ms against 12-17ms for the rest so the window opened because the machine was busy
Resolution: Recorded rather than tuned away; four rounds are run because more attempts catch more and widening the target to six units was tried and did not help. The guarantee rests on construction - the same lock on the same rows in the same ascending order applyInventoryEffect has used since CF-P0-006
Notes: Honest limitation of contention testing on an idle machine; the confirmation-layer oversell WAS reliably demonstrable which is why that suite is stronger evidence

Finding: Medicine withdrawal periods were not recorded anywhere so §35's eligibility check could not be written
Root Cause: medication_administrations recorded what was given and when and nothing about how long the animal must stay out of the food chain - selling inside a withdrawal period puts drug residue into food and is a regulatory matter for the farm
Resolution: Added withdrawal_period_days as read off the bottle and withdrawal_ends_on derived at write; PigListingEligibilityService blocks a push and a publish while a withdrawal is running and names the date it clears
Test: PigListingEligibilityTest 18 tests; removing the check fails 5 of them
Notes: A storefront that lists such an animal with one click makes it likelier not less which is why §35 puts the check at the push step

Finding: Health holds were not enforced when pushing a pig to the shop
Root Cause: §35 step 2 requires not under withdrawal/health hold and nothing consulted health records
Resolution: Unresolved severe or high severity conditions block as do planned or ongoing treatments; mild unresolved conditions deliberately do not because blocking on a healing scrape would make the check something staff route around

Finding: A per-kilo listing with no weight was only refused at the customer's cart
Root Cause: CartService rejects a per-kg listing with no weight as priced per kg but has no weight - correct but the staff member found out from a customer
Resolution: Eligibility blocks it at the push step so it is caught while the listing is being created

Finding: Eligibility was checked only when a listing was drafted
Root Cause: A listing drafted on Monday and published on Friday may have had a treatment recorded in between and withdrawal periods start after the paperwork not before
Resolution: ListingService::publish re-checks; checkListing filters out the already-on-the-shop blocker because the listing being published is itself that listing
Test: PigListingEligibilityTest test_a_treatment_recorded_after_drafting_stops_the_listing_publishing; removing the re-check fails it

Finding: A refusal that names one reason at a time sends a staff member hunting
Root Cause: Finding out about the withdrawal period waiting a fortnight and only then being told about the missing weight is the same information delivered as badly as possible
Resolution: check() returns every blocker and caution; the push wizard shows them when it OPENS not after the form is submitted and submit-time refusals render through the same block

Finding: The withdrawal enforcement only bites once someone records a withdrawal period and there is no field on the medication form yet
Root Cause: The column model and checks are storefront work; the operational recording UI is pig-operations work
Resolution: Closed in Phase 13b - the field is on the medication form with validation and an HTTP test
Notes: Anyone reading Phase 11 as withdrawal periods are now enforced should read it as the enforcement exists and is waiting on one input field

Finding: Storefront orders carry no tax at all so a VAT-registered farm selling online collects no VAT and under-declares it
Root Cause: storefront_orders has no tax column; StorefrontOrderConfirmedSubscriber sets no tax_code_id on the sale it creates so the resulting invoice has tax_total zero. §38 asks the checkout to show subtotal delivery tax total and it cannot
Resolution: BUILT in Phase 12b. storefront_orders pig_sales and feed_sales carry tax_profile_id tax_amount and a TaxCalculation snapshot; CheckoutService computes with the real TaxCalculator; the order's tax is apportioned across lines with the residual on the last so the parts sum to the whole; the pig path credits tax through InvoicePostingService and the feed path gains an explicit VAT line because it posts without an invoice
Test: StorefrontTaxTest 9 tests including an end-to-end proof that the tax charged is credited to the tax control account
Notes: Design recorded in PHASE_12 §5 including the governing test - what the checkout displays and what the invoice posts must be the same number

Finding: Blueprint §41's rule against direct GL posting in storefront code was stated in a document and enforced by nothing
Root Cause: A developer debugging something like IMP-044 - storefront sales silently failing to reach finance - is pushed toward exactly the wrong fix: post it here where you can see it work. That passes testing and double-posts the moment the subscriber runs
Resolution: Architecture test sweeps every storefront PHP file for PostingEngine JournalBatchDraft and direct JournalBatch/JournalLine creation; comments are stripped first so the docblock explaining the rule cannot fail the test enforcing it and the sweep asserts it found files so a directory move cannot make it pass silently
Test: StorefrontFinanceBoundaryTest test_no_storefront_code_posts_to_the_general_ledger_directly; adding a PostingEngine import to CheckoutService fails it

Finding: Storefront settlement discrepancies were detected but only ever reported to a cron log
Root Cause: finance:reconcile-storefront-settlements computes them correctly and deliberately reports rather than acts but a treasurer looking at the finance screen could not see that a payment had been verified at the gateway and never reached the books
Resolution: NeedsAttentionService surfaces them - paid but not posted as CRITICAL and awaiting payment over a day as INFO because ranking the two together would train people to ignore both; the detail text carries the command's own warning not to resubmit to the provider
Notes: Closes the remaining half of IMP-027

Finding: A feed sale would have charged the buyer tax that never reached the ledger
Root Cause: Feed revenue posts straight to the GL rather than through an invoice so unlike the pig path there is no InvoicePostingService to credit the tax account - the farm would hold money it had not recorded as owed to the revenue authority which is worse than charging no tax
Resolution: FeedSaleRevenueSubscriber debits the customer for the gross credits revenue for the net and credits VAT control for the difference and only when there is tax so untaxed farms are untouched; same account the invoice path credits so both land in one place
Test: StorefrontTaxTest test_the_tax_charged_reaches_the_ledger; removing the VAT line fails it

Finding: Apportioning an order's tax across its lines by independent rounding does not sum to what the buyer was charged
Root Cause: Three lines of 33.33 at 20% round to 6.67 each - 20.01 against an order tax of 20.00 - so the buyer is charged one number and the invoices total another
Resolution: StorefrontTaxService::allocate gives the last line the residual so the parts sum to the whole exactly; delivery's share rides on the lines proportionally rather than becoming a phantom delivery line on one invoice

Finding: A backgrounded MariaDB gate run reported exit 0 with no output because the server had shut down mid-session
Root Cause: The 11.4.2 server process is reaped when its parent shell exits - the same failure MARIADB_11_4_GATE_FINDING documents - and the runner script exits 0 when it cannot connect
Resolution: Recorded: check the gate produced TEST COUNTS not just an exit code. The empty output is what gave it away; the server was restarted and every result re-measured against a live server
Test: Pending a runner that fails loudly on no connection
Notes: A gate that reports success without running is worse than one that fails

Finding: My own down() dropped a foreign key by a hand-built constraint name where Laravel expects a column list
Root Cause: Passing the name produced <table>_<table>_tax_profile_id_foreign_foreign which does not exist so the drop silently did nothing and SQLite then refused the column drop
Resolution: Dropped by column and split the constraint drop from the column drop into two statements; found by RUNNING the rollback rather than assuming it worked
Test: Rollback and re-apply verified on SQLite and MariaDB 11.4.2

Finding: There is no screen for requesting a return - §43 step 1 is user requests return/refund with reason and quantity and route:list matches nothing
Root Cause: Returns are recorded by RecordSalesReturnService which is reachable only from the storefront refund path and from tests
Resolution: BUILT in Phase 13b - Finance > Returns records through RecordSalesReturnService with §45's indivisible pig rule and the no-auto-restock rule enforced in the controller

Finding: A credit note reversed no tax at all so a return would strand the VAT the buyer paid
Root Cause: CreditNoteService hard-coded tax_total to 0.00 - honest while sales carried no tax but Phase 12b made storefront sales charge VAT so the farm would keep tax on goods that came back while the customer was credited the net having paid the gross
Resolution: reversedTax scales the ORIGINAL TaxCalculation snapshot by the return proportion rather than recomputing from today's profile (IMP-014); a sale with no snapshot reverses nothing which is correct
Test: SalesReturnRevenueTest test_a_return_credits_the_tax_that_was_charged plus 6 unit tests; hard-coding the reversal back to zero fails it
Notes: §44 named this as future work - Phase 12b turned it from a gap into a defect

Finding: The credit note posting would have debited the whole gross to revenue
Root Cause: With tax now in line_total debiting all of it reduces income by more than was ever earned - the tax was never income it was money held for the revenue authority
Resolution: Revenue is debited NET and a separate line debits VAT control for the tax mirroring how InvoicePostingService credits it on the way out; untaxed returns do not touch the account at all which matters because a farm with no tax has no VAT control account to resolve

Finding: A negative control for the tax reversal broke nothing when the defect was reintroduced
Root Cause: The unit tests exercised reversedTax() and buildPostingDraft() separately and nothing touched the line in ensureForSalesReturn() that joins them - a guard nothing exercises is not a guard
Resolution: Added an end-to-end test in tests/Feature/Finance/SalesReturns where the fiscal period and chart-of-accounts fixtures already exist rather than duplicating that scaffolding; the same defect now fails loudly
Notes: Second time in two phases that reintroducing a defect proved a test weaker than it looked

Finding: The withdrawal-period field is now on the medication form so Phase 11's guard can finally fire
Root Cause: IMP-090 - the enforcement was built and correct but no form field existed so every treatment recorded read as no withdrawal
Resolution: One number input validated nullable|integer|min:0|max:365; nullable because most treatments carry none and guessing a default would block legal sales and teach people to ignore the warning; capped at 365 because a number beyond a year is a typo not a medicine; help text says what it does
Test: PigListingEligibilityTest test_a_withdrawal_period_recorded_on_the_form_blocks_a_sale drives the real HTTP path; dropping the field from validation fails it
Notes: Closes IMP-090

Finding: The return-request screen is built so §43 step 1 has a surface
Root Cause: IMP-098 - RecordSalesReturnService validated recorded and raised the credit note but was reachable only from the storefront refund path and from tests
Resolution: Finance > Returns records through the service and posts nothing itself; a pig has no quantity field because §45 makes returns indivisible and the controller passes 1 without reading the request; a returned pig never restocks because §45 requires a staff health decision first
Test: SalesReturnScreenTest 8 tests; making a pig return divisible or removing the cross-org check fails them
Notes: Closes IMP-098

Finding: Recording a return needed its own permission rather than borrowing the storefront refund one
Root Cause: refund_storefront_orders was closest but this screen covers direct farm-gate sales that never touched the storefront so borrowing it would tie the ability to record a return to whether the farm sells online
Resolution: record_sales_returns granted to admin superuser and accountant - deliberately NOT salesperson because the person who made the sale should not be the only one who can reverse it

Finding: Ten advanced finance feature flags gated nothing so every advanced URL stayed live regardless of configuration
Root Cause: Phase 1 defined twenty features and only eight gated a route; FinanceNavigation hid the menu entries while the URLs remained - prompt §110 says a disabled feature must not remain usable via URL
Resolution: Gated eleven advanced surfaces against the flags FeatureCatalog's own backs field names - chart of accounts journals trial balance vendor invoices payment runs supplier statements WHT bank statements reconciliation period close year-end investors biological assets and costing
Test: AdvancedFeatureGatingTest 24 tests; removing a gate fails one
Notes: Deferred here from Phase 7 onward because gating them piecemeal would leave a worse half-state than either end

Finding: Gating could have made a feature flag the only thing between a user and a ledger
Root Cause: SEC-001 requires feature enabled AND permission granted AND organisation scope valid; adding feature middleware invites someone to drop the permission middleware as redundant
Resolution: Half the new test file asserts that every gated surface with its feature ON still refuses a user who lacks the permission

Finding: The SEC-001 control did not work at first - dropping a route's permission middleware left it green
Root Cause: The outer finance.access boundary refuses a user holding no finance permission at all so the test could not tell the route checked from the boundary caught it
Resolution: The user now holds record_expenses - the narrowest real finance permission - enough to clear the outer boundary and entitling them to no ledger; removing a per-route permission now fails loudly
Notes: Third time in four phases that reintroducing a defect exposed a test weaker than it looked

Finding: Turning the gates on broke 54 existing tests
Root Cause: Every one exercised a surface that is off by default for a NEW organisation while the fixtures represent established farms
Resolution: FinanceTestSetup enables the whole catalogue because that fixture is an established accounting organisation and Phase 1's backfill gives such an organisation everything; a test ABOUT gating switches a feature off deliberately. FinanceRouteAuthorizationTest needed the opposite treatment - features explicitly ON so a 404 cannot mask whether the permission check ran
Test: Full suite 1723 green on both engines

Finding: The admin order page showed the finance posting outcome nowhere so a confirmed order whose sale never reached the books looked identical to one that posted cleanly
Root Cause: Phase 4 added finance_posting_status and finance_posting_error to the order and rendered neither; Needs Attention counted such orders but a count on a dashboard does not say which order or why
Resolution: The order page is now §46's recovery console - failed shows the error and offers a replay skipped is explained rather than reported as a failure and held stock shows what is held until when and what resolves it
Test: OrderRecoveryConsoleTest 9 tests; removing the panel fails three of them
Notes: §46 names the admin order page explicitly as the recovery console

Finding: A failed finance posting had no replay path so the only recovery was database access
Root Cause: §46 step - finance posting failed then replay event after fixing cause - had no surface
Resolution: retryFinancePosting returns the outbox event to pending and posts nothing itself; the outbox does the work and every posting downstream is guarded by journal_postings.idempotency_key so a replay of work that already succeeded writes no second journal; offered only for an event that actually FAILED because re-queueing a processed event is a no-op that looks like an action
Notes: The button says it is safe to press twice because a staff member unsure whether the first press worked will press it again

Finding: The negative control for the replay filter broke nothing when the defect was reintroduced
Root Cause: replayableEventFor has two guards - the order must not be posted AND the event must have failed - and the existing test only exercised the first because the posted short-circuit caught its case anyway
Resolution: Added a test isolating the filter - an order whose lines were SKIPPED (not an error so not posted either) with an event that processed successfully; removing the STATUS_FAILED filter now fails
Notes: Fourth time in five phases that reintroducing a defect exposed a test weaker than it looked - two guards in one method with one test is the shape to watch for

Finding: AdminOrderController answers 403 for a cross-tenant miss where the rest of the programme answers 404
Root Cause: assertSameOrg has aborted 403 for every action in that controller since it was written
Resolution: Not changed here - the retry follows the file's existing convention rather than diverging mid-file; prompt §118 prefers 404 so another farm's records stay undiscoverable and changing it alters every action on the controller
Test: OrderRecoveryConsoleTest test_another_organisations_order_cannot_be_retried asserts the current 403 with the reasoning in a comment
Notes: Belongs in its own change with its own tests not smuggled into a UX phase

Finding: The recovery panel was hidden from a user who can view orders but not manage them
Root Cause: It went in under @can('manage_storefront_orders') alongside the existing action forms so an order clerk would see a perfectly normal-looking order with a sale missing from the books - the exact dead end the panel exists to close recreated by the permission check
Resolution: Split by what each thing is - the STATE follows view_storefront_orders because knowing something is wrong is not a privileged act while the RETRY needs manage_storefront_orders enforced on the route; the button is hidden from someone who could not use it because a button that answers 403 is a worse dead end than no button
Test: OrderRecoveryConsoleTest test_retrying_requires_the_permission_to_manage_orders; removing the @can around the button fails it
Notes: Found by writing the permission test not by review

Finding: §55's viewport review across the older ledger screens is not done
Root Cause: The screens this programme built are mobile-first; the pre-existing ledger screens predate that and were not in this phase's state audit
Resolution: Still open after Phase 17. §60's Mobile row asks for browser/screenshot checks and Laravel Dusk is not installed - adding a browser-driver harness is a larger change than that phase warranted so it is named as not done rather than quietly counted; Phase 17's class-safety sweep catches a real defect class screenshots would likely miss but says nothing about whether a screen is usable at 390px
Notes: Scope now precise - a viewport review of the older ledger and dashboard screens which predate this programme's mobile-first work

Finding: A farm manager created through the application was refused the finance overview that §49 grants them while a legacy user on a role row nobody can hold kept it
Root Cause: manager and farmmanager are one product role under two row names - User::normalizeRoleName maps the former to the latter and manager is absent from ALLOWED_ROLE_NAMES so no user the application creates can hold it; the 25 permission seeders had settled into three conventions about which name to grant to (alias one to the other / grant to both / grant to manager alone) and the rows drifted
Resolution: One shared convention NormalizesSeededRoleNames applied to every permission seeder so a seeder may keep writing the farm's vocabulary while the grant lands on the row a user can hold; plus an idempotent re-runnable migration that copies the legacy row's grants onto farmmanager BEFORE moving users across so nobody loses access in the gap
Test: PermissionMatrixTest 11 tests and ManagerRoleReconciliationTest 6 tests; removing the normalization fails 5 including the concrete 403
Notes: Measured before touching anything - farmmanager GET /finance 403 vs manager 200; permission grants are silent when they miss which is why this survived fifteen phases

Finding: FinanceNavigation - the feature-and-permission-aware finance menu Phase 3 wrote - was referenced by nothing but its own tests so the live sidebar was still 240 lines of hardcoded role arrays that ignored organisation feature flags
Root Cause: IMP-070 recorded this as two menu builders in parallel; a repository sweep found the correct one was dead code and the wrong one was live so Phase 3's menu and Phase 14's gating both passed their tests while the running application did neither
Resolution: NavigationHelper's Finance section now delegates to FinanceNavigation through a thin adapter that only translates shape - the decisions stay in one place; a farm on Essentials is no longer offered Vendor Invoices and Chart of Accounts in a sidebar that answers 404
Test: FinanceSidebarTest 5 tests; bypassing the builder fails 4
Notes: Closes IMP-070. After Phase 14 the menu was manufacturing the §46 dead end the programme keeps closing

Finding: The Needs Attention cards for failed finance postings and stuck outbox events were gated on view_finance_dashboard which no seeder anywhere creates so they were invisible to every user except superuser
Root Cause: The permission existed only in two NeedsAttentionService card definitions and one FinanceNavigation entry; while FinanceNavigation was unwired the mistake could not be seen and wiring it up made the Overview entry vanish for everyone which is how it was found
Resolution: All three now ask for view_finance which is what the route actually enforces - a menu must ask for the permission the page checks or it hides a page the user can reach
Test: FinanceOverviewScreenTest; the test that asserted the card was HIDDEN passed because nobody holds the permission so it was rewritten to exercise filtering against a card whose permission exists
Notes: The recovery queue Phase 3 built was correct and then gated on a permission that was never created - anyone relying on it to catch unposted sales saw an empty queue

Finding: mill_operator holds five permissions but is absent from ALLOWED_ROLE_NAMES so no user can hold the role
Root Cause: Same class as IMP-115 - a grant to a role name no user can hold reaches nobody
Resolution: NOT changed - all five permissions are also held by farmmanager and admin so nothing is unreachable and it is dead weight rather than a lockout; making it a real role is a product decision §49 does not cover
Test: PermissionMatrixTest lists it as a documented exception with the reasoning in the constant
Notes: If mill operators are to be real users they need a row in §49 first

Finding: Wiring FinanceNavigation up removed the entire inventory and costing area from the menu plus Balance Sheet Cash Flow Reclassification Cap Table and Allocate Profit
Root Cause: finance.costing.index is a route that has never existed and admits() silently drops entries whose route is unregistered; Reports Loans and Investors had no sub-entries at all so five screens had working routes and nothing linking to them
Resolution: Pointed the costing entry at the routes that exist (inventory.value group-pools opening-pig-inventory mortality-writeoffs account-mappings gr-ir-ageing) and gave Reports and Loans children; §25 says the ledger screens are kept rather than deleted and a screen with no link is deleted by another name
Test: FinanceSidebarNavigationTest 3 tests - every route assertion unchanged
Notes: None of this was visible while the class was dead code because nothing made it agree with routes/web.php

Finding: Period Close and Year End asked the menu for manage_period_close while both index routes require view_period_close
Root Cause: Same shape as IMP-117 - the menu demanded more than the page does so the screens were hidden from a farm manager entitled to read them
Resolution: Both entries now accept view_period_close

Finding: storefront_listings.reference had no unique index while storefront_orders and storefront_quotes both carry one
Root Cause: §47 names StorefrontReferenceAllocator as the control for all three series but only two tables had the database backstop; the allocator is a single serialised writer so a duplicate was unlikely but would have been accepted in silence
Resolution: Added UNIQUE (organization_id reference); the migration REFUSES with the duplicates named rather than repairing because a listing reference is printed and quoted to customers and choosing which row keeps the number is a business decision not a deploy-time one
Test: ListingReferenceUniquenessTest 5 tests including the rollback exercised rather than assumed
Notes: Nulls still repeated freely so listings predating the allocator are unaffected

Finding: Phase 15's retry button was never proved to reach the claimer
Root Cause: Its tests asserted the event's status column changed; a button that sets a column and is never collected again would have passed all of them
Resolution: End-to-end tests prove a re-queued dead letter is claimed and processed; also pinned the one-press-one-attempt behaviour - a dead letter arrives with its attempt counter at the ceiling so a replay that fails again dead-letters immediately rather than climbing the backoff ladder a second time

Finding: Five templates build Tailwind class names by interpolation so those utilities were never generated and the elements render correctly classed and entirely unstyled

Resolution: Safelisted the eight colour names the controllers actually emit against the utility/shade pairs the views interpolate; verified by building the CSS both ways rather than inferring - without the safelist bg-pink-100 is MISSING from the compiled stylesheet
